subject: Remote comp alignment: COLA stipend for EU/APAC offers
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, michael.grant@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Riley Chen <riley@talentpartners.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: COLA stipend recommendation for Manila candidate

Team —

Short version: recruiter is pushing to close Sofia Martinez (Sr. Infra Eng, remote from Manila). Market comps show base slightly under target for our band. Recruiting requests a one-time COLA stipend (months 1-3) OR a small base uplift to align. Need leadership OK for a localized, time-limited stipend as an exception.

Why: Philippines inflation and the local offer market skew mean she would expect ~12% uplift vs our US-equivalent band to accept. Hiring manager prefers stipend to avoid band cascades.

What I need from you today:
- Quick decision on stipend vs base uplift (recruiter prefers stipend).
- Approval amount (suggested 10% one-time or 6% ongoing base uplift).
- Confirmation we can route through payroll for one-time payment and mark as non-recurring.

I've attached a quick comp model (comp_model_2027.xlsx) and the draft offer (candidate_offer_draft.pdf). Riley, can you confirm candidate timeline?

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Global Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, michael.grant@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: COLA stipend recommendation for Manila candidate

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and the files. I looked at the comp_model tab; high-level thoughts:
- I prefer a one-time stipend for this role rather than a base uplift to avoid setting a permanent precedent across the EU/APAC remote cohort.
- Proposed concrete: 9% one-time gross stipend (paid in payroll month 1). If hiring manager insists, we can escalate to 11% but need sign-off from Finance.
- If we go stipend route, recruiting should include clear language in the offer: one-time, non-recurring, taxable, not part of base.

Two asks for the hiring flow:
1) Vanessa, can you confirm whether payroll can process a one-time gross payment to an international contractor/employee in PH and the tax reporting implications?
2) Riley, candidate timeline (how long before offer needs to hit)?

If payroll confirms by EOD, I can approve up to 10% and Michael can do final sign-off for anything above.

-Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference
From: benchmarks@acme-analytics.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, michael.grant@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Riley Chen <riley@talentpartners.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:08:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Request: COLA stipend recommendation for Manila candidate

Hi team,

We ran quick peer benchmarking for senior infra roles remote in PH and EU. Highlights attached (acme_market_benchmarks.pdf):
- Median local-adjusted comp for Sr Infra Eng (remote PH) is ~8-12% above US-equivalent band when normalized for total cash.
- For EU-remote (senior infra in lower-cost EU markets), median uplift is ~5-9%.
- Recommendation: If you want to preserve base bands but remain competitive, implement a one-time gross COLA stipend equal to 9% of annualized base for APAC candidates in the Philippines and 6% for lower-cost EU remote locations.

Notes on framing: one-time stipend reduces downstream pressure on managers to raise bands; however, it must be documented as non-recurring in offer letters and HR systems.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the model.

Best,
Acme Analytics (benchmarks team)
